title: Rate-conditioned NN asymmetry did not improve frozen heart-failure classification across PhysioNet collections
abstract: We tested whether the slow-minus-fast difference in five-minute deceleration-energy asymmetry adds information beyond standard NN variability and median block asymmetry. L2 logistic models were fitted in 82 recordings (28 CHF, 54 NSR) from chf2db/nsr2db and frozen for testing in 33 recordings (15 CHF, 18 NSR) from chfdb/nsrdb. Adding the contrast increased Brier loss from 0.084267 to 0.100140; difference +0.015873 (conditional 95% stratified bootstrap interval +0.004193 to +0.028803). Resampling training and test subjects widened the interval to -0.008856 to +0.055677. AUROC fell from 0.955556 to 0.937037. A small leave-one-out development gain did not transfer. Bounds, block-duration, regularization and rate-dispersion checks did not establish benefit. These are cross-database source-label predictions, not clinical diagnosis. Prior investigator exposure, unlinked participant identities, demographic and acquisition differences limit confirmation. Reproducible code, input hashes and author self-checks are provided.
